prompt: hpx::future destructor blocking behavior vs std::future
answer:
- **`std::future`:** Its destructor may block when all of the following are true: the shared state was created by `std::async`, it is not ready, and the future is the last reference to that state. In other cases, destructors do not block. ([cppreference](https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/thread/future/~future), [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/standard-library/future?view=msvc-170))

- **`hpx::future`:** Its destructor does **not** conditionally block in this way. HPX deliberately chose not to conform to the standard behavior because implicit blocking—especially in destructors—is error-prone and interferes with HPX’s user-space scheduling. ([P0701R1](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2017/p0701r1.html))

Thus, unlike `std::future` from `std::async`, an `hpx::future` destructor is non-blocking.
